title: A modified CUT&RUN-seq technique for qPCR analysis of chromatin-protein interactions
protocol: Grow 4-5 million cells in a 10 cm dish format.

Reseed mES cell culture to stimulate proliferation one day prior to transfection for cultures displaying 80%-90% confluency, reseeding approximately 1/4 of cells; for cultures displaying 40%-60% confluency, reseed approximately 1/3 of cells.
Harvest cells and count viable cells under the microscope using trypan blue exclusion and a hemocytometer on the day of transfection.
Dilute 10 μL of cell suspension into 90 μL trypan blue to count cells.
Calculate the cell concentration by multiplying the number of counted cells by 10,000 and considering the dilution factor of 10.
Resuspend mES cells in mES cell media to a density of 0.8 million cells/mL.
Cover the wells of all the 24-well plates with 0.5 mL of PBS/gelatin (0.2% gelatin in 1× PBS) and incubate the plates for at least 5 min at room temperature to gelatinize.
Aspirate the PBS/gelatin and plate 200 μL of 0.8 million cells/mL mES cell suspension (160,000 cells) to each well immediately after gelatinizing.
Add 0.5 μg plasmid in 33 μL Opti-MEM per reaction in a 5 mL polystyrene tube.
Agitate the tube by gently flicking it to mix.
Mix 1.2 μL of Lipofectamine 2000 with 33 μL Opti-MEM per reaction in a 5 mL polystyrene tube.
Agitate the tube by gently flicking it to mix.
Incubate both plasmid and Lipofectamine mixes at room temperature for 5 min.
Transfer one equal volume of Lipofectamine mix to each plasmid mix to set up the lipofection reactions.
Agitate each 5 mL reaction tube by gentle flicking or pipetting using a p1000 pipet.
Incubate the lipofection reactions at room temperature for 5–10 min.
Transfect target wells by transferring 70 μL of the appropriate lipofection reaction to each designated well.
Flick each lipofection mix gently before addition.
After adding the lipofection reaction, gently agitate the 24-well plate being careful not to swirl the contents of the wells.
Place the 24-well transfection plate in a humidified tissue culture incubator at 37°C for 6 h.
Gently add 1 mL mES cell media to each transfected well using a 25 mL pipet, taking care to avoid touching any individual well’s contents with the pipet tip.
Return the plate(s) to the tissue culture incubator for overnight incubation.
Remove mES cell media from each well.
Add 500 μL 1×PBS to wash each well and decant the PBS.
Incubate cells in 100 μL 0.25% trypsin/EDTA at 37°C for 3 minutes.
Tap plates firmly to loosen adherent cells from plastic and break up cell clumps.
Add 100 μL DMEM/EDTA to each well, swirl wells to mix.
Harvest cells using p1000 tips by pipetting four-five times per well.
Count viable cells using trypan blue exclusion and a hemocytometer.
Aliquot 1 million cells per condition in mES cell media into Eppendorf tubes.
Wash cells twice with sterile 1×PBS, pelleting at 600 × g for 3 minutes.
Remove every last drop of the PBS supernatant after the second wash.
Gently resuspend Concanavalin A (ConA)-coupled magnetic beads by slow inversion.
Calculate the volume of beads needed (10 μL per sample).
Transfer this volume of beads to a 2.0 mL tube containing chilled 1.5 mL Binding Buffer.
Mix the tube contents by inversion.
Place the tube on a magnetic separator for approximately 30 seconds.
Remove the supernatant using a p1000 pipette after the liquid clarifies.
Repeat the binding buffer wash for a total of two washes.
After the second wash, resuspend the beads in a volume of binding buffer equal to the initial volume of bead suspension (10 μL per final sample).
Place the cell-bead suspension on ice.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL wash buffer.
Pellet cells in a microfuge at 600 × g for 3 minutes at room temperature for each wash step.
Add 1 mL wash Buffer following the second wash.
Resuspend cells using a p1000 pipette.
Add 10 μL of prepared ConA bead slurry to each sample.
Resuspend cells thoroughly by pipetting to prevent ConA bead clumping.
Place samples on Benchmark Nutator Mixer for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Check that the contents of each tube are moving and mixing well.
Supplement rocking by gently agitating samples using a p1000 pipet if necessary.
Place Eppendorf tubes on a magnet stand until the fluid is clear.
Remove the liquid carefully using a p200 pipet to remove every last drop of liquid.
Add 400 μL of chilled freshly prepared Antibody buffer.
Resuspend ConA bead/cell conjugate from the wall thoroughly by gentle mixing using a p1000 pipet.
Transfer entire contents to a 0.5 mL low binding tube.
Add 3 μL of antibody to each tube.
Mix using a p1000 pipet.
Incubate samples on the Nutator rocking platform at 4°C overnight.
Resuspend cells attached to ConA beads thoroughly by pipetting before incubating samples overnight.
Wash cells twice in chilled digitonin buffer.
Flick each tube to consolidate contents and place samples on magnetic separator for approximately 30 seconds.
Remove supernatant using a p1000 pipet.
Add 500 μL of chilled Digitonin Buffer and mix beads thoroughly by inversion.
Use a p200 pipet to remove every last microliter of liquid after the second wash.
Add 350 μL of chilled digitonin buffer and mix each sample gently using a p1000 pipet.
Add 2.5 μL of pAG-MNase and mix each sample gently using a p1000 pipet.
Place each sample on Nutator for 30 minutes at room temperature to allow pA/G-MNase-antibody chromatin binding.
Expose samples to calcium to activate MNase and cleave chromatin on either side of the targeted protein.
Release cleaved fragments by allowing them to diffuse out of the immobilized nuclei.
Wash cells two times with 400 μL chilled digitonin buffer by inverting tube  3–4 times.
Remove every last μL of liquid after second wash using a p200 pipet.
Add 300 μL chilled digitonin buffer and 3 μL chilled 100 mM CaCl2 to activate MNase.
Mix samples using a p1000 pipet as fast as possible.
Rock samples on a Nutator at 4°C for 4 h.
Preheat thermomixer with 1.5–2 mL smart block to 37°C.
Transfer each sample to a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 100 μL chilled stop buffer to each tube and gently mix using a p1000 pipet.
Place samples on thermomixer set to 500 rpm at 37°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge samples at 16,000 × g at 4°C for 10 min.
Place the tube on a magnet stand and transfer supernatant to a 2 mL tube once beads concentrate.
Extract DNA from the supernatant using a Qiagen MinElute PCR purification Kit following manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute purified DNA in 20 μL of elution buffer.
Store purified samples at −20°C.
Assess the concentration of the eluted DNA sample using a Nanodrop Spectrophotometer.
Run qPCR of all samples using a qPCR machine with 3 technical repeats per experimental repeat.
Establish the melting curve properties to determine the specificity of the PCR reaction.
Analyze the primer pair sequence to avoid complementarity and hybridization between primers.
Assess the homogeneity of the PCR products by analyzing the dissociation curve for each primer, expecting a single sharp peak.
Use the 2–ΔΔ CT method to analyze the CUT&RUN-qPCR data.
Use empty vector-transfected cells as an untreated control sample.
Select a control genomic locus distant from the Ter array.
Choose sequences in the β-actin gene for the control locus.
Subtract the CT value at the Ter locus from the CT value at the β-actin locus for samples transfected with Tus.
Subtract the CT value at the Ter locus from the CT value at the β-actin locus for empty vector-transfected samples.
